requirements.condition: A receiver receives a higher-numbered stream ID with intervening streams of the same type not yet open.
requirements.required_behavior: The receiver opens every intervening stream of that same type.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The receiver must not leave any intervening stream of the same type unopened.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can deliver a higher-numbered stream ID and inspect whether all lower intervening stream IDs of the same type become open.

requirements.condition: Stream 4000000 is opened on a new connection as a client-initiated bidirectional stream.
requirements.required_behavior: The connection has 1 million and 1 client-initiated bidirectional streams opened as a consequence.
requirements.why_checkable: The stated stream-number example gives an exact expected count that can be checked after processing the opening stream.

requirements.quote:
The number of active streams is limited by the
   initial_max_streams_bidi and initial_max_streams_uni transport
   parameters as updated by any received MAX_STREAMS frames, as
   explained in Section 4.6.  If chosen judiciously, these limits
requirements.condition: An endpoint determines how many streams may be active, including after receiving MAX_STREAMS frames.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint limits active streams according to initial_max_streams_bidi and initial_max_streams_uni, with those limits updated by received MAX_STREAMS frames.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The endpoint must not allow the number of active streams to exceed the applicable updated limit.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can configure the initial transport parameters, deliver MAX_STREAMS frames, and verify that active-stream admission follows the resulting limits.
